answer: Each identity binds one distinct address in the velvet registry: the registrar mails a code there; activation needs it key-signed with a 60-credit bond. One address backs one identity, so each fake needs a new address. The k-th address costs 30 plus 5(k-1) credits; the 1,000th costs 5,025, and 1,000 fakes pay 2,527,500 plus 60,000 bonds. At dawn the registry logs debuts; at horizon it reconciles each address to one key, burning duplicates' bonds. Rented addresses fail: forwarded codes map many keys to one address, rejected at horizon. Honest agents pay once; bond returns after a clean epoch.
